vulnerability.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
vulnerability.description: Vulnerabilities that allow attackers to inject client-side scripts
vulnerability.impact: Can lead to session hijacking, credential theft, or delivery of malware to users
vulnerability.mitigation: Apply context-aware output encoding, use Content-Security-Policy, validate and sanitize all inputs

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
findings.explanation: Unescaped output to HTML can lead to XSS vulnerabilities. The `transfer` function is used directly with user input without proper sanitization.
findings.impact: Potential session hijacking or credential theft via an intermediary contract
exploitation_steps: User sends a malicious tx to the contract with an amount containing JavaScript code
findings.remediation: Use a safer function like `transfer() { require(tx.origin == owner); }` or sanitize user input before passing it to the `transfer()` function

findings.title: Vulnerability found
findings.vulnerable_code: function CashOut(uint _am) public payable { if(_am<=balances[msg.sender]) { // <yes> <report> REENTRANCY if(msg.sender.call.value(_am)()) { ... } } }
findings.explanation: The use of msg.sender.call.value() with user input allows an attacker to inject arbitrary JavaScript code.
findings.impact: Can lead to session hijacking, credential theft, or delivery of malware to users
findings.execution_path_diagram:
CashOut(_am)
  - msg.sender.call.value(_am)
    - execution of user-provided code
findings.remediation: Use msg.sender.call.value with strict encoding (e.g. encode(_am) instead of _am)
findings.secure_code_example: function CashOut(uint _am) public payable { if(_am<=balances[msg.sender]) { balances[msg.sender] -= _am; } else { require(_am == 0); } }

findings.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability
findings.explanation: Using msg.sender.call.value() with a user-input variable _weiToWithdraw allows an attacker to inject malicious JavaScript code.
findings.impact: An attacker could steal sensitive data or perform unauthorized actions on behalf of the user.
exploitation_steps: An attacker sends a request to /withdrawFunds with a malicious _weiToWithdraw value containing JavaScript code.
findings.exploitation_conditions: The user is authenticated and the withdrawal amount is sufficient.

chunk_analyses.notes: This contract uses a vulnerable function call to allow user-input values to be executed as JavaScript code.
